chapters.heading: User guide

subsections.heading: How to cite the source data
subsections.html:
Cite the MCS deposits used to build the file, and acknowledge the Centre for Longitudinal Studies (CLS), UCL, following current CLS citation guidance.

Deposits used:

  • MCS Sweep 1 (SN 4683)
  • MCS Sweep 2 (SN 5350)
  • MCS Sweep 5 (SN 7464)
  • MCS Sweep 6 (SN 8156)
  • MCS Sweep 7 (SN 8682)
  • MCS Sweep 8 (SN 9509)
  • MCS Longitudinal Family File and related files (SN 8172), including the cohort-member longitudinal file and the MCS Core dataset

Sweeps 3 and 4 are not used in this file.

chapters.html:
Version 1.0

This user guide describes a cohort-member-level teaching file derived from the Millennium Cohort Study (MCS). It covers how the file was constructed, the survey design variables, the treatment of missing data, and the coding of every released variable.

The file is for teaching. It remains UK Data Service End User Licence data. Do not share it outside the licence under which the source deposits were obtained.

subsections.heading: 1.1 The Millennium Cohort Study
subsections.html:
MCS follows a nationally representative sample of people born in the United Kingdom in 2000-02. Eight sweeps are used as the source for this file:

Sweep Typical age Fieldwork began
MCS1 9 months 2001
MCS2 3 years 2004
MCS5 11 years 2012
MCS6 14 years 2015
MCS7 17 years 2018
MCS8 23 years 2023

subsections.heading: 1.2 What this file contains
subsections.html:
The class file is a single wide dataset. Each row is a cohort member. Identifiers are mcsid (family or household research ID) and cnum (cohort member number within the family: 1, 2 or 3). Twins and triplets are retained.

The file contains:

  • identifiers and survey design variables
  • sweep issued, outcome and response flags
  • sex at birth and ethnic group
  • parent-reported SDQ conduct problems at age 3
  • self-reported delinquency, delinquent attitudes, jobs, online time, dating, victimization, gang membership, weapon carrying, criminal justice contact, living arrangements, partnership, NVQ and full-time work, as specified in Section 5

It does not contain names, addresses, school identifiers or other disclosive fields from the source deposits.

subsections.heading: 1.3 Files on disk
subsections.html:
File Contents
mcs_class.dta Stata 14 file
mcs_class.csv Same observations and variables, no value labels

N in the class file is 19,505 cohort members.

subsections.heading: 2.1 Software
subsections.html: The file is built in R using haven and tidyverse. haven::read_dta is used for all Stata source files, including those with Latin-1 labels.

subsections.heading: 2.2 Longitudinal File
subsections.html: The longitudinal data file mcs_longitudinal_cm_file.dta is used to track individuals through waves. Twelve cases with data_availability = 0 are dropped because they are not licensed for research use. No other cases are deleted. Cohort members who missed later sweeps remain on the file with missing values on those sweeps. More information is in the CLS longitudinal family file guide.

subsections.heading: 2.3 Source files and merge keys
subsections.html:
All merges are one-to-one on mcsid and cnum. Wave-specific person numbers (ECNUM00, fcnum00, gcnum00, hcnum00) are renamed to cnum. Variable names are converted to lower case after reading.

Role File Why this file
Spine, design, weights mcs_longitudinal_cm_file.dta One row per cohort member; issued flags and sweep weights
Sex, ethnicity, age 3 SDQ score mcs_core.dta Sex at birth and first-recorded 11-category ethnicity; parent SDQ conduct score at sweep 2 already at cohort-member level
Age 3 SDQ items mcs2_parent_interview.dta Five conduct items; family-level a0/b0/c0 mapped to cnum 1/2/3
Age 11 items mcs5_cm_interview.dta Child self-completion
Age 11 chores mcs5_parent_cm_interview.dta Parent report of household chores (EPACHM00); main interview preferred
Age 14 items mcs6_cm_interview.dta Young person CASI
Age 17 items mcs7_cm_interview.dta Young person interview and self-completion, all cohort members
Age 23 items mcs8_23y_cm_survey.dta Cohort member survey
Age 23 derived mcs8_23y_cm_derived.dta Marital status, cohabitation, economic activity, NVQ

mcs7_cm_interview_onlyCM1.dta is not used. It drops second and third cohort members. mcs7_cm_vars_only.dta is not used as the primary source.

A small number of interview records belong to the 12 cases with data_availability = 0 (3 at MCS5, 7 at MCS6, 2 at MCS7). Those records are not on the spine and are not in the class file.

Forty-five cohort members on the spine are absent from mcs_core.dta. They are kept. Sex, ethnicity and the age 3 conduct score are missing for those cases unless another source supplies them.

subsections.heading: 2.4 Recode Rule
subsections.html:
Unless a specific rule is given in Section 5:

The MCS missing codes are converted to system missing (NA in R, . in Stata). Typical missing codes in the source files are -1 (not applicable), -3 (not asked at this fieldwork stage), -8 (don't know or insufficient information) and -9 (refusal or prefer not to say). At MCS7 some don't know, refuse and no-answer codes are positive (3 to 6). Those positive missing codes are also set to system missing. Negative survey weights (CLS placeholders for non-productive cases) are set to system missing, following the CLS advice in the MCS Stata analysis guide.

Yes/No items are recoded to 1 = Yes, 0 = No. NVQ code 96 retained; gang "used to be" coded as No; SDQ cut at 4; no non-positive analysis weights.

No case is dropped because an item is missing.

subsections.heading: 3.1 Design
subsections.html:
MCS is a stratified, clustered sample of children born in the UK over a 16-month period from 2000. Electoral wards (later grouped into superwards) were the primary sampling units. The sample over-represents wards with high child poverty and, in England, wards with a high proportion of ethnic minority families.

Unweighted percentages in this file do not represent the UK birth cohort.

subsections.heading: 3.2 Design variables in the class file
subsections.html:
Variable Role
country Country at sampling: 1 England, 2 Wales, 3 Scotland, 4 Northern Ireland
pttype2 Stratum within country (advantaged, disadvantaged, and, in England, ethnic)
sptn00 Primary sampling unit (fieldwork point / superward). Stored as the deposited character code.
nh2 Population correction factor supplied by CLS
weight1, weight2, weightgb Base MCS weights for single-country, whole-UK and Great Britain analyses
eovwt1, eovwt2, enrespwt MCS5 (age 11) overall single-country, overall UK, and non-response weights
fovwt1, fovwt2, fnrespwt MCS6 (age 14) equivalents
govwt1, govwt2, gnrespwt MCS7 (age 17) equivalents
hovwt1, hovwt2, hovwtgb, hnrespwt MCS8 (age 23) equivalents
eissued, fissued, gissued, hissued Issued at that sweep
eaoutc00, faoutc00, gaoutc00, haoutc00 Official outcome codes
hcasetype MCS8 case type
resp11, resp14, resp17, resp23 1 if the cohort-member interview or survey used in this file is present

pttype2 codes:

Code Stratum
1 England, advantaged
2 England, disadvantaged
3 England, ethnic
4 Wales, advantaged
5 Wales, disadvantaged
6 Scotland, advantaged
7 Scotland, disadvantaged
8 Northern Ireland, advantaged
9 Northern Ireland, disadvantaged

Overall weights (*ovwt*) combine the sample design weight and a non-response adjustment. The *nrespwt variables are the non-response component. Do not use a non-response weight on its own as the analysis weight.

subsections.heading: 3.3 Which weight to use
subsections.html:
Analysis Restrict to Weight (UK) Weight (one country)
Age 11 item resp11 == 1 eovwt2 eovwt1
Age 14 item resp14 == 1 fovwt2 fovwt1
Age 17 item resp17 == 1 govwt2 govwt1
Age 23 item resp23 == 1 hovwt2 hovwt1
Great Britain only at age 23 resp23 == 1 and country in 1-3 hovwtgb

If a model uses predictors from an earlier sweep and an outcome from a later sweep, use the overall weight for the outcome sweep and state that earlier-wave attrition is only partly adjusted.

subsections.heading: 3.4 Example: setting the design
subsections.html:
R, age 14, whole UK:

library(haven)
library(survey)
mcs <- read_dta("mcs_class.dta")
des14 <- svydesign(
  ids     = ~sptn00,
  strata  = ~pttype2,
  weights = ~fovwt2,
  fpc     = ~nh2,
  nest    = TRUE,
  data    = subset(mcs, resp14 == 1)
)
svymean(~delinq14_shoplift, des14, na.rm = TRUE)

Stata, same design:

use mcs_class.dta, clear
svyset sptn00 [pweight=fovwt2], strata(pttype2) fpc(nh2) singleunit(centered)
svy, subpop(if resp14==1): mean delinq14_shoplift

nh2 may be omitted if a finite population correction is not required. singleunit(centered) (Stata) or equivalent handling of singleton strata is recommended because some strata can have few remaining points after attrition.

Respondent counts in the class file:

Flag N
resp11 13,436
resp14 11,719
resp17 10,343
resp23 9,675

chapters.heading: 4. Missing data
chapters.html:
The file is not restricted to complete cases. Three kinds of missingness appear in MCS and are treated as follows.

Unit non-response and attrition. A cohort member who was not issued, or who did not complete the relevant interview, stays on the file. Items from that sweep are system missing. resp11 to resp23 identify who has that interview. Issued and outcome codes are kept so that attrition tables can be produced.

Item non-response and explicit missing codes. Don't know, refusal, prefer not to say, no answer, not applicable and "not asked at this fieldwork stage" are converted to system missing. They are not recoded to No and they are not given a separate missing category in the class file.

Routing. Some items are asked only if a previous item takes a given value. Job hours at 17 are asked of those in work. Court appearance at 17 is asked of those who report an arrest. In the class file a skipped item is system missing, except for the composite cj17 (Section 5.22), which uses the gate items so that "no arrest and no caution" is coded No rather than missing.

Special codes that are not missing. nvq23 code 96 ("None of these qualifications") is a valid substantive code and is retained. Gang code 3 ("I used to be a member but am not any more") is recoded to No (not currently a member), not to missing.

Weights. Negative weights are set to system missing. They mark non-productive cases and must not enter a weighted analysis.

subsections.heading: 5.4 Conduct problems at age 3 (SDQ)
subsections.html:
Parent-completed Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, 2-4 year version, main parent. The official score is the sweep-2 conduct score, derived by CLS from items temper tantrums, generally obedient (reversed), fights or bullies, argumentative with adults, and spiteful. Scoring follows sdqinfo.org parental 2-4 year rules. Score range 0-10.

Field Detail
Class variable conduct3_score
Original variable conduct at sweep 2
Original codes 0-10. Missing: -1 and blank
Recode 0-10 retained
Field Detail
Class variable conduct3
Recode 1 if score is 4-10 (high band for ages 2-4); 0 if score is 0-3
Notes The 2-4 year banding is: 0-2 close to average, 3 slightly raised, 4-10 high.
Code Label N
0 No (score 0-3) 9,982
1 Yes (score 4-10) 4,956
Missing 4,567

The five source items are also released as Yes/No. Family-level MCS2 columns (a0/b0/c0) are mapped to cnum 1/2/3.

Field Detail
Original codes 1 Not true; 2 Somewhat true; 3 Certainly true; 4 Can't say
Recode Problem items: Yes if Somewhat true or Certainly true. conduct3_disobedient is the reverse of "generally obedient": Yes if Not true or Somewhat true. Can't say (4) and not applicable are missing.
